added_lines: . a christian as a dual citizen every christian has a dual citizenship. we are citizens of our various countries and yet at the same time citizen of god’s kingdom. this comes with privileges and obligations for each one and therein lies the challenge. there should be no conflict between being faithful christian and being a good citizen of our countries. when however, there is a sinful or unjust policy in any society, christians are called to take up the posture of conscientious objection. we should at that moment, uphold the dignity of our conscience. jesus’s answer to them, admonishes his adversaries and us to worry less about what is due to ceasar, to pay attention to god and worship that is duehim. the tax we must pay to god, if we are to belong to him kingdom, is to offer our heart, our spirit, soul, family and the society god, in a purposeful, meaningful, god-fearing manner. again, the gospel text today, teaches us that, all exercise of authority and power must be evaluated in the light of god’s will and plan. if ceasar is subservient to god, then his laws and policies will be in accord with god’s will. carrick-on-shannon (kiltoghert)
